Subject: Embedding handoff: preflight & vectorstore compatibility checks

Hi Tim / ACME Eng —

Thanks for the window this quarter. We're kicking off the handoff for embeddings + rerank migration and want to lock the preflight checklist and schedule before we start any heavy backfill. High-level goals: lower-latency rerank path in front of your search layer, no user-facing downtime, and a staged backfill with clear acceptance criteria.

Quick proposed plan (short):
- Preflight: compatibility check for your vectorstore, sample ingestion, and small-scale rerank eval (3 days)
- Dry-run backfill (staging): incremental seed of 10% of documents (1 day)
- Full backfill: batched bulk + ongoing incremental (scheduled 6–12 hour windows)
- Acceptance: rerank eval metrics (p@5, MRR, latency 95th pct) and smoke queries

Action items / owners:
- ACME Eng: confirm vector DB (type/version) + whether bulk import is available (owner: Tim)
- Marissa (Redwood): compatibility matrix and backfill sizing recommendations (attached playbook)
- Rishi (Redwood): rerank eval template + run smoke tests during dry-run
- Kimberly (Redwood): schedule kickoff call, coordinate JIRA ticketing / test tagging

Attachments: redwood_backfill_playbook_v1.md (playbook + sample scripts)

Can you confirm: (1) vectorstore type & version, (2) a preferred 6-hour maintenance window for full backfill (if needed), and (3) whether you want us to do the ingestion or have ACME run the bulk import?

I'll propose a 30-min kickoff tomorrow at 11am PT unless you prefer a different time.

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Embedding handoff: preflight & vectorstore compatibility checks

Thanks Kimberly — appreciate the clear plan. A few immediate notes/questions: 

1) Our current vectorstore is Pinecone (v1.14.x) for production and a small Milvus (2.2) cluster for staging. We can perform bulk imports via our internal ETL but would prefer Redwood to run the backfill script in staging first.

2) Downtime: we prefer zero-downtime for search; but if a 6-hour window is required for the full backfill, target Sunday 02:00–08:00 PT.

3) Rerank evals: can you confirm what thresholds you recommend for pass/fail? For example, we'd like <2x token-cost increase and MRR improvement >= 5% over current baseline.

Happy to join the kickoff tomorrow. 11am PT works for me.

—Tim
Head of Search, ACME Corp

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Dec 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Embedding handoff: preflight & vectorstore compatibility checks

Great context — thanks Tim. A few technical clarifications and recommendations from the implementation side: 

Compatibility notes:
- Pinecone v1.14.x: supported (we've validated dynamic upserts and namespace-based isolation). Bulk import through Pinecone's import job is fine.
- Milvus 2.2 (staging): supported with the standard gRPC client; watch out for segment merge pauses during heavy writes.

Backfill approach (recommended):
1) Seed + incremental: run an initial seed of 10% with KV caching enabled (to warm prefix cache).
2) Observe rerank quality on that slice for 48 hours.
3) Full bulk backfill in staged batches (we recommend batches of 50k vectors/hour for Pinecone — adjust if you hit I/O limits).

Operational knobs to avoid regressions:
- Batch sizing and concurrent write threads (start at 8 threads, monitor write latency).
- Quantization profile: if ACME uses <8-bit quant, share quant profiles — Redwood can recommend a compatible QAT profile to reduce storage/cost.

Acceptance criteria (we've attached a template):
- p@5 uplift >= 4% relative to baseline OR MRR uplift >= 5%
- Rerank latency P95 < 120ms for production routing (measured from query arrival to model score)
- No more than a 1.5x increase in average per-query token cost during steady-state (exclude heavy backfill windows)

Attachments: rerank_eval_template.xlsx — includes test corpus, queries, expected metrics, and a sample scoring script.

Dry-run suggestion: 2026-12-20 run in staging upsert of 10% (dataset id: acme-staging-seed-2026) — we can run smoke queries and push results into the attached template.

I'll own the compatibility checklist and will post results to the Drive link Kimberly shared.

—Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Adding a few operational points and next steps from the rerank/eval perspective: 

- I'll run the smoke test harness during the dry-run and record p@1/p@5/MRR and latency buckets. I will tag results in JIRA:SUP-4821 and put artifacts in the shared Drive.
- For the smoke harness, please find the baseline queries and dev scoring in attached ACME-MAP-2026.pdf (mapping doc).
- If ACME prefers Redwood to perform ingestion in staging, we need temporary API keys from eng@acmecorp.com that expire after 24 hours. Otherwise provide the Pinecone import job credentials and we will validate post-import consistency.

Proposed timeline:
- 12/20: Dry-run seed (10%) — Redwood runs smoke tests same day
- 12/21–12/22: Evaluate metrics, iterate on batch sizing
- Week of 12/26: Full backfill windows (Sunday nights) — finalize exact windows after dry-run

I'll attach the smoke harness logs once the dry-run completes.

Rishi Malhotra
